security.factor.or: or a code from your authenticator app
security.factor.appFirst: or confirm with a passkey below
security.factor.recoveryHint: Format xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx. Each code works exactly once.
security.factor.wrongDetail: Codes change every 30 seconds; check the time of your phone too.
security.factor.recoveryWrong: This recovery code is not valid.
security.factor.recoveryWrongDetail: Check the spelling; each code works only once.
security.factor.passkeyCancelledDetail: The dialog was closed, or this device has no matching passkey. Try again or use a code.
security.factor.passkeyUnavailable: This browser cannot use passkeys here.
security.factor.locked: Too many wrong codes. Locked until {time}.
security.factor.lockedDetail: Then it works again. If you can no longer use the app, an admin can reset your second factor.
security.signIn.title: Confirm it’s you
security.signIn.lead: Second step of signing in. Use a method you have set up.
security.signIn.expired: The sign-in has expired. Sign in again.
security.signIn.recoveryUsed: Signed in with a recovery code.
security.signIn.recoveryLeft: You have {count} codes left. Make new ones under Account > Sign-in and security before they run out.
security.setup.title: Set up a second factor
security.setup.leadOrg: {org} requires a second factor for your account. Then you go straight on.
security.setup.leadServer: This server requires a second factor for your account. Then you go straight on.
security.setup.passkeyHint: Fingerprint, face, device PIN or a security key. Nothing to type.
security.setup.appHint: A six-digit code from an app on your phone.
security.setup.later: You can add more methods later under Account > Sign-in and security.
security.setup.passkeyLead: Follow the dialog of your browser or device.
security.totp.scan: 1. Scan the code with your authenticator app.
security.totp.manual: No scanner? Type the key by hand:
security.totp.wrong: The code does not match the key. Wait for the next code and check the time of your phone.
security.totp.expired: The setup has expired. Start it again.
security.codes.title: Your recovery codes
security.codes.lead: Visible only now. Kalzit stores them only as a hash.
security.codes.note: Each code stands in once for your second factor, for example when your phone is gone. Keep them apart from your password.
security.codes.saved: I have stored the codes safely
security.account.required: A second factor is required for your account.
security.account.requiredOrg: Set by the organization {org}. You can add and swap methods; the last one cannot be removed.
security.account.requiredServer: Set by this server. You can add and swap methods; the last one cannot be removed.
security.account.protect: Protect your account with a second factor: a passkey or an authenticator app.
security.account.locked: Locked until {time} after too many wrong codes.
security.account.appSince: Set up on {date} · last used on {used}
security.account.appSinceUnused: Set up on {date} · not used yet
security.account.passkeysLead: Sign in with fingerprint, face, device PIN or security key.
security.account.codesMeta: {remaining} of {total} left · made on {date}. The codes are shown only when they are made.
security.account.codesNone: They come with the first method.
security.account.appSaved: The authenticator app is set up.
security.account.codesMade: New recovery codes made; the old ones no longer work.
security.dialog.confirmFirst: Confirm with your second factor first.
security.dialog.passwordText: A new password weakens what protects your account, so Kalzit asks for your second factor first.
security.dialog.passkeyNameHint: So you recognize it later, such as “Office laptop”.
security.dialog.lastText: “{name}” is your last method for the second factor. A second factor is required for your account; set up another one first.
security.dialog.removeText: You can set it up again later.
security.dialog.regenText: Your {count} remaining codes stop working then.
security.admin.label: Second factor
security.admin.missingHint: sets one up at the next sign-in
security.admin.resetRemoves: Removes the authenticator app, passkeys and recovery codes.
security.admin.resetNext: At the next sign-in, {name} sets up a new one if one is required.
security.admin.resetAudit: The reset is in the audit log; {name} gets an email once a mail server is set up.
security.admin.confirmOwn: Admins cannot reset their own second factor here.
security.admin.ownMissing: Set up your own second factor first; only then can you reset the second factor of others.
security.admin.resetDone: The second factor of {name} was reset.
security.admin.needsServerAdmin: This account also belongs to other organizations or is a server admin; only a server admin can reset it.
security.policy.perOrgLead: Organizations may be stricter than the server, not laxer. Organization admins set this in their organization’s settings.
